mainTopic: Who receives a seduced girl's payments, and whether a court ruling turns a קנס into ordinary money for the קרבן שבועה.
overview: This amud finishes the משנה: a girl's earnings and found items go to her brothers if the father dies, even if nothing was collected. The גמרא asks why the משנה lists the seducer's payments at all, since an earlier משנה already taught them. It answers that the point is that they go to the father. It then pushes back that this is obvious too. The final answer is that the משנה is needed for עמדה בדין, a case tied to a dispute between רבי שמעון and the רבנן. The גמרא brings that dispute from מסכת שבועות. רבי שמעון exempts a man who falsely swore he did not seduce or violate, because a קנס is not paid on one's own admission. אביי asks רבה whether a court ruling turns the קנס into ordinary money, and רבה says it does. אביי then challenges him with a ברייתא of רבי שמעון that excludes fines from the קרבן שבועה, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The last line of the משנה: her earnings and finds go to the brothers
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by ruling that a daughter's earnings and found items belong to her brothers once the father dies, even if they were never collected.
steps.simpleTranslation: Her earnings and the things she found, even if she has not collected them yet: if the father dies, they belong to the brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the משנה. It says that what the girl earns or finds already belongs to her father, so after his death it passes to her brothers as part of his estate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the משנה, the payments for seduction depend on whether she had already gone to court (עמדה בדין). Here the rule is simpler. מעשה ידיה and מציאה belong to the father from the moment they come into being, so collecting them does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: Her earnings, meaning what she makes from her work

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the seduction payments earlier in the משנה. For those, timing and court matter. For earnings and finds, the brothers inherit even if nothing was collected.

phrases.english: Her earnings and the things she found,
even though she has not collected them,

phrases.aramaic: מֵת הָאָב — הֲרֵי הֵן שֶׁל אַחִין.
phrases.english: if the father died, they belong to the brothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final clause of the משנה, continuing its list of what belongs to the father.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A daughter's earnings and finds belong to the father, so they pass to the brothers at his death even if not yet collected.

steps.title: Why repeat the seducer's payments? We already learned them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: we already know from an earlier משנה that a seducer pays בושת, פגם and קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the משנה teaching us? We already learned: the seducer pays three things and the rapist four. The seducer pays for humiliation, degradation and the fine, and the rapist adds a payment for pain!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking what is new in our משנה. It points out that the payments of a מפתה were already listed in an earlier משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says the בושת, פגם and קנס of a seduced girl go to her father. The גמרא assumes the משנה is mainly telling us that these payments exist. Since that was already taught (כתובות 39a), the משנה looks repetitive.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? (asked when something seems already known)
A seducer (the relationship was with her consent)
Payments for humiliation, for her loss of value, and the Torah's fixed fine
Pain, paid only by the אונס

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is it teaching us?
We already learned: The seducer pays three things,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in כתובות 39a.

phrases.english: and the rapist pays four.
The seducer pays for humiliation, degradation, and the fine;

phrases.aramaic: מוֹסִיף עָלָיו אוֹנֵס שֶׁנּוֹתֵן אֶת הַצַּעַר!
phrases.english: the rapist adds to this, since he also pays for the pain!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to the גמרא's first question about it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for our משנה to list the seducer's payments.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An earlier משנה already taught that the מפתה pays בושת, פגם and קנס, so repeating it adds nothing.

steps.title: The new point: the money goes to her father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה's new point is who receives the money: the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed to teach that the money goes to her father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is not just listing the payments again. It is telling us that they go to the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה only said what the seducer pays. Our משנה adds who collects those payments. That would be enough reason for the משנה to repeat the list.

phrases.english: It was needed to teach that it goes to her father.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a new point in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה was only listing the payments again.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is teaching who receives them: the father.

steps.title: That the money goes to the father is also obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: of course the money goes to the father, because a girl who consented could not claim payment for herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: That it goes to her father is also obvious, from the fact that a seducer pays at all. If the money were hers, why would a seducer pay? He acted with her consent!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the last answer. Even the point that the money goes to the father is obvious and did not need teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מפתה acted with the girl's agreement, so she has no claim against him herself. The only reason he pays is that someone else, her father, was wronged. So the earlier משנה already implies that the payment goes to the father.

phrases.english: That it goes to her father is also obvious,
from the fact that a seducer pays;
for if the money were for her, why would a seducer pay?
He acted with her consent!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה teaches the money goes to the father.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מפתה only pays because someone other than the consenting girl was wronged. So the father must be the one who collects, and that is obvious.

steps.title: The real point: the case where she already went to court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is needed for the case of עמדה בדין, which is disputed by רבי שמעון and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed for the case where she stood in judgment, which is a dispute between רבי שמעון and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer. The משנה's real new teaching is about timing: what happens if she went to court while her father was alive, but he died before the money was collected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה rules that if she went to court while the father was alive, the payment is his, so the brothers inherit it even though it was never collected. The גמרא says this case touches a dispute between רבי שמעון and the רבנן, which the earlier משנה does not show. The next steps bring that dispute from מסכת שבועות, about whether a קנס counts as real money for a false oath.

keyTerms.meaning: She stood in judgment: the court case was already decided

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה is not repeating the seducer's payments. Its new teaching is the case of עמדה בדין: once she went to court in the father's lifetime, the brothers inherit even if nothing was collected. The גמרא ties this to a dispute between רבי שמעון and the רבנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a court ruling can be enough to make the money the father's, even before he collects it. That idea leads into the discussion of רבי שמעון's view that follows.

phrases.english: It was needed for the case where she stood in judgment,
phrases.notes: She went to court while her father was alive, but he died before collecting.

phrases.english: which is a dispute between Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4 and closes the question opened in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the משנה's focus to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to teach only obvious things: what a seducer pays and that it goes to the father.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is teaching the timing rule of עמדה בדין, a point that רבי שמעון and the רבנן dispute.

steps.title: A משנה from שבועות: a man falsely swore he did not seduce or violate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in which a father accuses a man, the man denies it under oath, and later admits. He is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה there: A father says, 'You raped or seduced my daughter.' The man says, 'I did not rape and I did not seduce.' The father says, 'I make you swear,' and he answers 'Amen.' Afterward he admits it. He is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in a new source, a משנה from מסכת שבועות. This step sets up the next discussion: the גמרא is preparing to examine what this ruling means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a false oath about money: the man swore he owed nothing for seducing or violating the girl, then admitted he did. The משנה rules simply that he is חייב. Exactly which payments it means is what the coming lines will explore.

keyTerms.meaning: I make you swear (I put you under oath)

phrases.english: We learned there: "You raped or seduced my daughter,"
phrases.notes: שבועות 36b. Literally 'and', but he means one or the other.

phrases.english: and he says: "I did not rape and I did not seduce."
"I make you swear," and he said: "Amen,"
and afterward he admitted, he is liable.
phrases.notes: The משנה there means he must pay, plus the extra penalties for a false oath about money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by bringing in a related משנה from מסכת שבועות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who swore falsely that he did not seduce or violate a man's daughter, and later admitted it, is liable.

steps.title: רבי שמעון exempts the swearer, and the רבנן respond
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון exempts the man who swore falsely, because a קנס is not paid on one's own admission. The רבנן answer that בושת and פגם are paid on one's own admission.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says he is exempt, because a person does not pay a fine based on his own admission. The רבנן said to him: True, he does not pay the fine on his own admission, but he does pay for humiliation and degradation on his own admission.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה from step 6 continues. רבי שמעון disagrees and exempts the man, and the רבנן answer him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A false oath only brings a קרבן שבועה if the person denied something he would have to pay had he admitted it. רבי שמעון says a קנס is never paid on one's own admission, so denying it is not denying real money. The רבנן say that בושת and פגם are part of the claim and are paid on admission, so his oath did deny real money.

keyTerms.meaning: a fixed penalty set by the Torah, not ordinary compensation
on his own admission, with no witnesses
payment for humiliation and for loss of value

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon exempts him,
phrases.notes: He means the man does not bring the קרבן for a false oath.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם קְנָס עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: because he does not pay a fine on his own admission.
They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם קְנָס עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: Although he does not pay the fine on his own admission,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מְשַׁלֵּם בּוֹשֶׁת וּפְגָם עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: he does pay humiliation and degradation on his own admission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה quoted in step 6 by giving רבי שמעון's dissent and the רבנן's reply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון: no קרבן שבועה, since a קנס is not paid on admission. רבנן: he is liable, since בושת and פגם are paid on admission.

steps.title: אביי asks about a man who was already judged in court
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבה: if the father says the man was already judged and ordered to pay, and the man swears falsely and later admits, what is the law according to רבי שמעון?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked רבה: One says to another, 'You raped or seduced my daughter, I brought you to court, and you were obligated to pay me money.' The other says, 'I did not rape or seduce, you did not bring me to court, and I was not obligated to pay you money.' He swore and then admitted. According to רבי שמעון, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a new question built on רבי שמעון's view. The man's case already went to court before he swore falsely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון exempted the man because a קנס is not paid on admission. Here the court has already ordered payment, so the question is whether that changes anything. The two sides of the question come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: I brought you to court and you were judged

phrases.english: Abaye asked of Rabba:
One who says to his fellow:
"You raped or seduced my daughter,
and I brought you to court,
and you were obligated to pay me money,"
and he says: "I did not rape and I did not seduce,
and you did not bring me to court,
and I was not obligated to pay you money,"
and he swore and then admitted,
according to Rabbi Shimon, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבי שמעון's exemption from step 7 and tests it on a case where the court already ruled.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי שמעון still exempt the swearer when the court had already obligated him to pay?

steps.title: The two sides of אביי's question
steps.stepSummary: אביי lays out both options: once judged, it may count as ordinary money, or it may still be a קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he stood trial, it is money, and he is liable for an oath offering over it? Or perhaps, even though he stood trial, it is still a fine?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why he is unsure. He gives the reasoning for each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: the court ruling makes it an ordinary debt, so denying it is denying money and brings a קרבן שבועה. Option two: the payment keeps its nature as a קנס even after the ruling, so רבי שמעון would still exempt him.

keyTerms.meaning: the offering brought for a false oath denying a money claim

phrases.english: Since he stood trial,
it is money,
and he is liable for an oath offering over it?
Or perhaps,
even though he stood trial,
it is still a fine?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reasoning behind the question asked in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a court ruling change a קנס into ordinary ממון?

steps.title: רבה answers: once judged, it is money
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that after a court ruling the payment counts as ordinary money, so a false oath brings a קרבן שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is money, and he is liable for an oath offering over it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה picks the first side of אביי's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a court has obligated the man, he owes a regular debt, not just a קנס. So even רבי שמעון would agree that denying it under oath is denying money.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה: after עמידה בדין, a קנס is treated as ממון, even for רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: He said to him:
It is money,
and he is liable for an oath offering over it.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After a court ruling, the payment is ממון and a false oath brings a קרבן שבועה.

steps.title: אביי begins a challenge from a ברייתא of רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא in which רבי שמעון lists claims like rape, seduction, an ox killing a slave, and a slave's tooth or eye. The swearer denied and then admitted. The ברייתא suggests he might be liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised an objection: רבי שמעון says: One might think that if one says to another, 'You raped or seduced my daughter,' and he says, 'I did not'; or 'Your ox killed my slave,' and he says, 'It did not'; or his slave says to him, 'You knocked out my tooth and blinded my eye,' and he says, 'I did not'; and he swore and then admitted, one might think he should be liable...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts a challenge to רבה from a ברייתא. This step only sets it up; the ברייתא's ruling comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא opens with 'one might think he is liable', which signals it is about to reject that idea in רבי שמעון's name. אביי will use the ending to argue against רבה's answer in step 10.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
Rabbi Shimon says:
One might think: one who says to his fellow
"You raped or seduced my daughter,"
and he says: "I did not rape and I did not seduce";
"Your ox killed my slave,"
and he says: "It did not kill";
or his slave said to him
"You knocked out my tooth or blinded my eye,"
and he says: "I did not knock it out and I did not blind it,"
and he swore and then admitted,
one might think he should be liable —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against רבה's answer in step 10, using a ברייתא in רבי שמעון's name.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that, for רבי שמעון, a payment becomes ממון once the case was judged in court
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists claims to which רבי שמעון applies his exemption. אביי will use its ending, which comes next, to argue against רבה.

steps.title: The ברייתא brings the פסוק about false oaths
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers its own question by quoting the פסוק about a person who denies a money claim and swears falsely.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: "And he deals falsely with his neighbor about a deposit, or a pledge, or a robbery, or has oppressed his neighbor, or found a lost item and denied it, and swore falsely."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now quotes the פסוק it will use to answer its question about whether these claims bring a קרבן שבועה. This step sets up the reasoning that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 ended by suggesting the swearer might be liable. Now the ברייתא turns to the פסוק that creates the קרבן שבועה. That פסוק lists specific cases: a deposit, a pledge, a robbery, withheld wages, and a lost item. The next step will point out what all of these cases have in common.

keyTerms.meaning: "The פסוק teaches". This phrase introduces a פסוק that settles the question.
An item left with someone for safekeeping
A pledge, or money handed over, such as a loan or a business partnership
Withheld what he owed, such as a worker's wages

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"And he deals falsely with his neighbor in a deposit
or in a pledge, or in a robbery,
or has oppressed his neighbor.
Or he found a lost item and denied it
and swore falsely",

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that אביי quoted in step 11. Here the ברייתא brings its פסוק to answer its own question.
steps.raayaObject: Which kinds of claims bring a קרבן שבועה when someone denies them under a false oath
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 5:21–22, the list of money cases in the passage about false oaths

steps.title: Only money claims count, so fines are excluded
steps.stepSummary: Every case in the פסוק is ordinary money, so only money claims bring a קרבן שבועה. Fines like the rapist's and seducer's payments are excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as all these cases are special in that they are money, so too only things that are money are included. That leaves out these cases, because they are fines.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא concludes that the payments for rape, seduction, and the like do not bring a קרבן שבועה, because they are קנס and not ממון. This completes אביי's challenge to רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns a general rule from what the cases in the פסוק share: all of them are ממון. A קנס is not like them, so a false oath about it brings no קרבן. The ברייתא gives no exception for a case where the court has already ruled, so it seems to clash with רבה's answer in step 10 that a ruled-on fine counts as ordinary money.

keyTerms.meaning: "Just as these are special". This phrase learns a general rule from the shared feature of the listed cases.
Ordinary money owed, matching the loss one person caused another
A fine set by the תורה, not tied to the actual loss

steps.whatToRemember: According to this ברייתא, a קרבן שבועה applies only to denying ממון. A קנס, such as the payments of a rapist or seducer, is excluded. This seems to challenge רבה, who said a fine that a court has already ruled on counts as money.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not say these payments stop being קנס. It only rules that the special law of קרבן שבועה does not apply to them. Whether a court ruling changes that is taken up on the next amud.

phrases.english: Just as these are special
in that they are money,
so too, everything that is money is included.
These are excluded, because they are fines.
phrases.notes: "These" are the cases listed in the ברייתא back in step 11: rape, seduction, the ox killing a slave, and the slave's tooth or eye.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה אֵלּוּ מְיוּחָדִין שֶׁהֵן מָמוֹן, אַף כֹּל שֶׁהֵן מָמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the פסוק quoted in step 12 and finishes the ברייתא that אביי quoted against רבה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling in step 10 that once a court has ruled, a fine counts as ordinary money and a false oath about it brings a קרבן שבועה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא, following רבי שמעון, excludes rape, seduction, and similar payments from the קרבן שבועה because they are קנס. It does not say this changes after a court ruling. That seems to contradict רבה.
